t.1.72.1: On the very day that the king performed the excellent gift of cows, on that same day the valiant Yudhājit arrived.
t.1.72.2: The son of the king of the Kekayas, Bharata's own maternal uncle, having seen the king and asked after his welfare, spoke these words to him.
t.1.72.3: The king, lord of the Kekayas, out of affection has spoken of his welfare: those whose welfare you desire are at present in good health.
t.1.72.4: O lord of kings, O ruler of the earth, I wished to see my sister's son, and for that purpose I came to Ayodhyā, O delight of the Raghus.
t.1.72.5: But I, having heard in Ayodhyā that your sons had gone to Mithilā together with you for the sake of marriage, O lord of the earth,
t.1.72.6: "I have come in haste, wishing to see my sister's son." Then King Daśaratha, seeing his dear guest arrived,
t.1.72.7: Seeing him, worthy of worship, he honored him with the highest marks of respect. Then he spent that night together with his great-souled sons.
t.1.72.8: Then, at the auspicious hour called Vijaya, Rāma, having performed the auspicious wedding rites and accompanied by his brothers adorned with every ornament, went to the sacrificial enclosure, placing the sages at the front.
t.1.72.9: Placing Vasiṣṭha at the front, and the other great seers as well,
t.1.72.10: O king, O best among the finest of men, King Daśaratha, with his sons for whom the auspicious wedding-thread rites have been performed, awaits the giver of the brides.
t.1.72.12: Thus addressed by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, the supremely noble one, of great splendor and the highest knower of dharma, spoke these words in reply.
t.1.72.11: Indeed, all aims are fulfilled for both the giver and the receiver. Having performed this excellent marriage, take up your own duty.
t.1.72.13: What doorkeeper of mine stands in the way, and whose command is being awaited? What hesitation can there be in one's own house? This kingdom is as much yours as mine.
t.1.72.15: I am ready, and stationed at this altar I am waiting for you. Let the king make it free of obstacles; for what reason indeed is there delay?
t.1.72.14: O best of sages, my daughters, having completed every auspicious wedding rite, have come to the foot of the altar, shining like the blaze of a fire.
t.1.72.16: Then, having heard those words spoken by Janaka, Daśaratha brought in all his sons and also the hosts of sages.
t.1.72.17: King Janaka said to him who increased Kausalyā's joy: "This Sītā, my daughter, is your companion in dharma. Accept her, may good fortune be yours, and take her hand in your hand."
t.1.72.18: Lakṣmaṇa, come, good fortune to you! Accept Ūrmilā, who is offered by me, and take her hand; let no time be lost.
t.1.72.19: Having spoken thus to him, Janaka also addressed Bharata: "O delight of the Raghus, take the hand of Māṇḍavī with your hand."
t.1.72.20: And the righteous-souled lord Janaka said to Śatrughna as well: "O mighty-armed one, take with your hand the hand of Śrutakīrti."
t.1.72.21: All of you are gentle, and all of you have faithfully kept your vows; may you Kākutsthas be united with your wives, and let there be no passing of time.
t.1.72.23: Having circumambulated the fire, the altar, the king and the sages, the great-souled best of the Raghus, together with their wives, performed the marriage according to the ordinance, just as it had been prescribed.
t.1.72.22: Having heard Janaka's words, those four, abiding by the counsel of Vasiṣṭha, took the hands of the four maidens in their own hands.
t.1.72.24: From the sky there fell a great and brilliantly shining shower of flowers, accompanied by the resounding of celestial kettledrums and the sounds of songs and musical instruments.
t.1.72.25: Hosts of Apsarases danced, and the Gandharvas sang sweetly; at the wedding of the foremost of the Raghus, that was a wondrous thing indeed.
t.1.72.27: Then the delights of the Raghus, together with their wives, went to the royal tent, and the king too followed, watching them, accompanied by the host of sages and by his kinsmen.
t.1.72.26: While this was taking place, amid the resounding din of musical instruments, those mighty princes of great vigor walked three times around the fire and wedded their wives.
